meta: David Pierre Giottino Humbert de Superville, painter and writer, seated in a black cap in Jacobus Ludovicus Cornet's portrait of 1840.
about: The painter and writer David Pierre Giottino Humbert de Superville sits in a chair with a black cap on his head. Jacobus Ludovicus Cornet painted the portrait in 1840. Mrs. S.E. Kneppelhout van Sterkenburg-Drabbe of Utrecht gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Paintings hung salon-style and a crowd around a reclining Venus at Christie's Auction Room, a plate by Augustus Charles Pugin from Microcosm of London.
about: This plate from the series Microcosm of London shows Christie's Auction Room. A crowd stands in a high-ceilinged room with light from high windows. Paintings in ornate frames hang salon-style, with vaguely recognizable classical subjects: an Annunciation, an Adoration, a saint, a rider and a portrait. A reclining Venus is displayed on the auction stand, and in front of her is a lively, colorful crowd with detailed dress and caricatured faces. Augustus Charles Pugin made the plate around 1800.

meta: Madame Grand, later Talleyrand's wife, in Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun's portrait of 1783, the year after she reached Paris.
about: Catherine Worlée was born in India, the daughter of a French East India Company official, and married George Grand, a clerk of the British East India Company. In 1782 she moved to Paris, where as Madame Grand she became a popular courtesan with several powerful lovers. She later became the mistress and then the wife of the diplomat Talleyrand. Wikipedia says her beauty was recorded in this 1783 portrait by Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun.

meta: A hare, dead birds, artichoke, asparagus and fruit on a table in Frans Snijders's 1616 still life.
about: A hare and dead birds lie on a table with an artichoke and a bunch of asparagus. Beside them are a dish of strawberries, a tazza of grapes with peaches and plums, a Venetian-style glass and a jug. Frans Snijders painted this still life with dead game, fruit and vegetables in 1616. The Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Canaletto's view of the Grand Canal near the Cannaregio Canal, painted about 1738 and perhaps ordered by Joseph Smith.
about: Canaletto painted this view of the upper Grand Canal near the entrance of the Cannaregio Canal around 1738, and it may have been ordered by the English merchant and collector Joseph Smith. The viewer floats in the middle of the canal among gondolas and barges, with buildings along both banks. Wikipedia says it is a typical vedute painting of the kind Grand Tour travelers liked as a record of their stay in Venice. Many of the buildings still stand, among them Palazzo Flangini at the far left.

meta: Perugino's Noli Me Tangere, one of four predella panels of 1500 to 1505 showing moments when Christ's divine nature was revealed.
about: This panel, with three others, once belonged to a predella, the row of small narrative pictures under an altarpiece. A fifth panel, the Resurrection, is in the Metropolitan Museum in New York. The scenes show moments when Christ's divine nature was revealed, at his birth, his baptism, his talk at a well with a Samaritan woman, his resurrection and his appearance to Mary Magdalene afterward. This one is Noli Me Tangere, by Perugino. The painting that crowned the altarpiece has not been identified.

meta: A young woman in Turkish dress painted by Friedrich Amerling in 1838 and titled The Young Eastern Woman.
about: Friedrich Amerling gave this painting the provocative title The Young Eastern Woman, but the museum points out that the model is plainly not Asian and simply wears a Turkish costume. Rich fabrics and glowing light create an exotic mood, which the museum reads as a Western fascination with Oriental images and themes.
credit_line: Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund

meta: Ships safely home at a busy Dutch port in Willem van de Velde the Younger's Entrance to a Dutch Port, about 1665.
about: A busy Dutch port fills this painting of about 1665, with a wooden breakwater and several kinds of ships, details well known to Van de Velde, the son of a famous draftsman. Wikipedia says it evokes a clear sunny day in port with ships that have come safely home, and that it points to the Netherlands' mercantile power in the 17th century. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

meta: Fifty figures dance, flirt and rest in Gabriel Jacques de Saint-Aubin's Country Dance, painted about 1760 to 1762.
about: Fifty figures fill this scene, doing everything from dancing to sharing a mother's caress with a child. The Getty says Saint-Aubin took his idea from Watteau's fêtes galantes, in which elegant people entertain themselves in an idealized park, but gave it a rural subject. Country dances had become a popular summer pastime for Parisian society in the 1700s. Saint-Aubin was a tireless chronicler of his time and would surely have watched such dances.

meta: Two women and four children meet in the shade of tall trees in Ker Xavier Roussel's Nabis painting of about 1890.
about: A group of figures, presumably two women and four children, meet in the shade of tall trees while others walk along the grassy riverbank. Roussel was a founding member of the Nabis and the brother-in-law of Édouard Vuillard. Like them he loved Japanese prints, and he developed a style of radically simplified forms and strong, decorative color. The museum says his intimate views of daily life convey a mood of quiet feeling rather than a story.

meta: A woman smokes a pipe by the water on a summer evening while fireworks go off, in Ippitsusai Bunchō's print Beauties at the Seashore.
about: Ippitsusai Bunchō shows the popular subject of cooling off by the water on a late spring or early summer evening, which the willow suggests. The seated woman enjoys her pipe, a favorite pastime of women in Edo. In the background fireworks are set off from a small boat. The catalog dates the work between about 1765 and 1792.

meta: Innocence turns from Riches toward Love in Pierre-Paul Prud'hon's sketch of about 1804 for a painting finished by Constance Mayer.
about: Innocence, at the center, shows that she prefers Love, a cupid, to Riches, a woman in lavish Grecian robes holding out a chest of golden trinkets. Prud'hon complicates the parable with the poses. Innocence embraces Love but looks longingly back over her shoulder at Riches, which makes viewers wonder how final her choice is. He made this as a preparatory sketch for a larger painting to be finished by his friend and collaborator Constance Mayer.

meta: David Wilkie painted the annual May fair of his home village in Pitlessie Fair, at 19, in 1804.
about: Pitlessie Fair shows the annual May fair held in David Wilkie's home village of Pitlessie in Fife. He painted it in 1804, at 19, and it is one of his earliest works. It came two years before his breakthrough at the Royal Academy with The Village Politicians, and both show how strongly the Dutch and Flemish old masters of the 1600s influenced him. Its success let him move to London for the rest of his career. The Scottish National Gallery bought it in 1921.

meta: Hermanus Fock's self-portrait miniature of 1786, with a tall hat and a painting on an easel behind him.
about: The painter Hermanus Fock shows himself half-length, facing us, in a tall hat, with a painting on an easel behind him. The small picture belongs to the Rijksmuseum's collection of portrait miniatures and is dated 1786.

meta: A satyr sits by a stream in a sunlit forest in Célestin François Nanteuil's In the Forest of 1841.
about: Nanteuil's love of nature shows in the trees, grassy slopes and water bathed in late afternoon sun. In 1837 he wrote to a friend that he often spent hours looking at plants with large leaves like lace, tall grasses in ponds, and little flowers with thousands of colors embroidering the ground. The forest looks real, yet the painting includes a satyr, a half human, half goat figure seated on a stone near a stream. He painted it in 1841.
credit_line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Noah L. Butkin

meta: Mary hears the angel Gabriel in a room dominated by white, blue and red in Dante Gabriel Rossetti's Ecce Ancilla Domini!, 1849 to 1850.
about: Rossetti used a deliberately limited range of colors for this Annunciation. White, the sign of virginity, dominates, with strong blue, a color linked to Mary, and red for Christ's blood. The Latin title, Ecce Ancilla Domini, means behold the handmaiden of the Lord and comes from the first chapter of Luke, where Mary accepts the angel Gabriel's message. Rossetti first painted it in 1850, and it is now in Tate Britain.

meta: A design for chinoiserie wall panels showing Europeans in stylised Chinese landscapes by Daniel Marot, about 1700.
about: A wide central panel and two narrow side panels are flanked by pilaster strips, and each panel and each half of the dado shows an alternative suggestion for the decoration. The panels show Europeans in stylised Chinese landscapes: a party in the open at the left, a reception at the center and a group of hunters at the right. Rinceaux ornament decorates the ceiling cove. Daniel Marot made the design around 1700.

meta: Christ sits on a rock and teaches a crowd in Michel Lasne's Sermon on the Mount, an engraving of about 1590.
about: Christ sits in the foreground at the left on a rock with a halo around his head, his arms raised in open gestures as he teaches. A crowd of men listen and talk among themselves, with a forest of leafy trees behind them. At the right a valley opens with more figures in conversation, and a city on a hill and mountains lie in the distance. A flock of birds crosses the cloudy sky. Michel Lasne made the print around 1590.

meta: A bald beggar with a staff stands among thirsty people being given drink in Michael Sweerts's Quenching the Thirsty, 1646.
about: A group of thirsty people are given something to drink in an Italian setting, with a bald beggar holding a stick standing in the middle. A church on a hill in the background may be the church of Trinità dei Monti. The picture is one of a series on the seven works of mercy. Michael Sweerts painted it in 1646, and the Rijksmuseum bought it with support from its photo sales committee.
